original_content.knowledge_point: Computing the Acceleration of a Particle at a Given Moment Given Its Position Vector
original_content.problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+5t,\,2{t}^{4}-4{t}^{2}+t+1⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0.$
original_content.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}+5t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{4}-4{t}^{2}+t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨6{t}^{2}+6t+5,\,8{t}^{3}-8t+1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{t}^{2}+6t+5),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(8{t}^{3}-8t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨12t+6,\,24{t}^{2}-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=0,$ we substitute $t=0$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(0) & =⟨12(0)+6,\,24(0)-8⟩ \\  & =⟨6,\,-8⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(0)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(0)| & =|⟨6,\,-8⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
